question.problem: A rectangular parallelepiped has a volume of $125\,{\text{in}}^{3}.$ Using the method of Lagrange multipliers, determine the minimum sum of the lengths of its edges.
question.worked_solution:
Let $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ be the rectangular parallelepiped's length, width, and height, respectively. We wish to minimize the function

$$
f(x,y,z)=4x+4y+4z,
$$

subject to the constraint 

$$
xyz=125.
$$

Note that we also have the constraints $x>0,y>0,z>0.$

Let $g(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z),\,g(x,y,z)=125
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y,z),{f}_{y}(x,y,z),{f}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y,z),{g}_{y}(x,y,z),{g}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ \\ ⟨4,4,4⟩ & =\lambda ⟨yz,xz,xy⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4=\lambda yz \\ 4=\lambda xz \\ 4=\lambda xy\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first, second, and third equations by $x,y,$ and $z$ respectively, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x=\lambda xyz \\ 4y=\lambda xyz \\ 4z=\lambda xyz\end{aligned}
$$

This gives $x=y=z.$

Now, using the constraint equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}xyz & =125 \\ x(x)(x) & =125 \\ {x}^{3} & =125 \\ x & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is reached at the point $(5,5,5),$ and the minimum value is 

$$
f(5,5,5)=4(5)+4(5)+4(5)=60\,\text{in}.
$$

**Note:** It's easy to show that the obtained point is indeed the minimum (and not the maximum). To do that, we could compare the value of the function at this point with the value of the function at any other (arbitrary) point belonging to the domain. For example, 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(25,5,1) & =4(25)+4(5)+4(1) \\  & =121 \\  & >f(5,5,5).\end{aligned}
$$
